Facts: Wu (被告人吴某) participated in concealment and transfer of shares that were proceeds from illegal public deposit (非法吸收公众存款) crime. He concealed and transferred assets, falsified contracts, etc. The prosecution charges money laundering (洗钱) amount 52 million. So the crime is "洗钱罪" (money laundering). Also possibly "帮助犯罪分子隐匿、转移、变卖犯罪所得" which is part of money laundering. Also maybe "伪造公司印章、合同" could be "伪造公司印章罪" or "伪造文书罪". The facts mention forging contract signing dates. That could be "伪造公司印章罪" if they forged documents. However the core is money laundering. The question: "只写这部分事实直接支持的罪名". The facts include forging contract dates to hide assets. That is falsification of documents (伪造文书罪). Also the act of transferring shares to conceal assets is money laundering. Also possibly "非法吸收公众存款罪" but Wu is not the one who did illegal public deposit; he is aiding. The prosecution says he knew the assets were from illegal public deposit and concealed them. So the crime is money laundering. Also "帮助他人隐匿、转移、变卖犯罪所得罪" is the same as money laundering under Chinese law (刑法第191条). So we list "洗钱罪". Should we also list "伪造文书罪"? The facts: "伪造合同签订日期". That's falsifying a contract, which is a false document. Under Chinese law, forging a contract is "伪造公司印章罪" if using company seal, or "伪造国家机关公文罪" if state. But forging a private contract is "伪造文书罪" (刑法第277条). So that could be a separate charge.

Thus we have two crimes: Money laundering (洗钱罪) and forging documents (伪造文书罪). The question: "用法定罪名". So we need the official Chinese crime names: "洗钱罪" and "伪造文书罪". Use semicolon.

Thus answer: [罪名]洗钱罪;伪造文书罪<eoa>
